newsitem.title: JAPAN: SKI JUMPING-GERMANY'S THOMA SOARS TO HILL RECORD.
newsitem.headline: SKI JUMPING-GERMANY'S THOMA SOARS TO HILL RECORD.

text.p: Germany's Dieter Thoma soared to a hill record of 134.5 metres in steady snow on Sunday to claim his fourth World Cup victory of the season.

Thoma, second after a first round jump of 121.5 metres, sailed past the previous record of 128 metres on his second attempt at the Okurayama large hill in Sapporo, northern Japan, to collect a winning total of 263.3 points.
It was the 11th World Cup win for Thoma, a member of Germany's gold medal winning team at the 1994 Lillehammer Olympic Games and winner of the normal hill bronze medal there.
"That was a super jump and I could have reached 140 metres if I hadn't thought of style points," an elated Thoma said.
The victory raised Thoma's World Cup points total to 774, narrowing the gap with leader Primoz Peterka of Slovenia. He has 832 points but is skipping the four-event, two-week Japan series.
Norway's Roar Ljokelsoy led with a first-round jump of 126 metres and added a second of 127 but had to settle for second place with 259.4 points.
Japan's Takanobu Okabe, the 1995 world normal hill champion, posted jumps of 117.5 and 129 metres for third.
With four jumpers finishing in the top 10, Japan preserved their comfortable lead in the World Cup nations' standings with 2,116 points. Finland are second with 1,719 and Norway third with 1,627.
